notes: Sequence correlation rules evaluated over the normalised case timeline. A correlation is reported as a HYPOTHESIS: entity links (same file name, same hash, process lineage via PID/parent PID, indicator embedded in an analysed binary) make it stronger, temporal proximity alone makes it weaker. Correlations never create events; every step references an existing timeline event.

rules.title: Downloaded executable was subsequently executed
rules.description: A browser download of an executable is followed by a process-creation event for an image with the same file name.

rules.title: Suspected intrusion chain: delivery, execution, sensitive data access and outbound transfer
rules.description: An executable delivered by download appears on disk, is executed, files in a sensitive location are accessed, and an unusually large outbound transfer to an external address follows, all on the same host within the correlation window.

steps.name: exfiltration
steps.description: Large outbound transfer to an external address

rules.title: Persistence created by a process descended from a downloaded executable
rules.description: After a downloaded executable runs, a scheduled task, service or local account is created whose action points into the executable's process lineage.

steps.name: execution
steps.description: Executable from a user-writable path launched

rules.title: Archive staged then large outbound transfer
rules.description: An archive file is created and a large outbound transfer to an external address follows from the same host.

rules.title: Event log cleared after suspicious execution
rules.description: An event log is cleared on a host after suspicious process execution was recorded there.
